meta.title: Change Language | ProxMenux Documentation
meta.description: Choose from eight ProxMenux interface languages. Every installation includes pre-generated JSON translation catalogs; no translation service or Python environment is needed on the host. The menu reloads automatically.
meta.ogDescription: Pick one of eight ProxMenux interface languages from Settings. Available on every installation.

header.title: Change Language
header.description: Switch the ProxMenux interface between eight supported languages. The choice is saved to config.json and the menu is restarted in the new language. Every installation includes the translation catalogs.

intro.title: What this is
intro.body: A dialog lists the eight supported languages. ProxMenux saves your choice to config.json as .language, then restarts config_menu.sh so it takes effect immediately.

warn.title: Available on every installation
warn.body: Settings always shows Change Language. Translation catalogs are installed in /usr/local/share/proxmenux/lang/, and the selected language is stored in config.json. No legacy Python translation environment is required.

englishTip.title: English is the most accurate
englishTip.body: Non-English text comes from pre-generated JSON catalogs included with ProxMenux. Missing translations fall back to English; there is no live translation call on the host. English remains the reference when a translation seems incorrect.

underHood.heading: How it works under the hood
items: The dialog lists eight language codes; choose one.
If config.json exists: jq --arg lang "$new_language" '.language = $lang'' updates the field in place.
If config.json doesn't exist: a fresh one is created with the language code in a single-field object.
exec bash config_menu.sh reloads the Settings menu with the new language active.

troubleshoot.heading: Troubleshooting
troubleshoot.noOptionBody: Change Language is always available in current releases. If it is missing, update ProxMenux using the official installer and open Settings again.
troubleshoot.stillEnglishTitle: Language changed but UI still shows English
troubleshoot.stillEnglishBody: The menu re-execs itself after the change. If you opened a fresh shell and started a different ProxMenux entrypoint, run menu again to pick up the new language. Confirm: jq -r '.language' /usr/local/share/proxmenux/config.json.
